title: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence Service Feasibility in Pediatric Infectious Diseases
summary:
In the study EASY-PID, the use of an artificial intelligence (AI)-supported telemedical consultation service for children and adolescents with infectious diseases is to be investigated.

On the one hand, as previously common, treatment recommendations for requests from external clinics are to be prepared by a resident physician ± pharmacist, reviewed and, if necessary, corrected by a pediatrician specialized in infectious diseases, and transmitted to the external treating team. In addition, and without use in patient care, treatment recommendations are to be prepared using a specifically trained and exclusively locally operating artificial intelligence. These recommendations are reviewed and again, if necessary, corrected by a pediatrician specialized in infectious diseases. The different consultation responses are to be evaluated by independent reviewers, enabling a statistical analysis on quality as well as efficiency.

interventions.name: Arm 1: Prospective generation of teleconsultations for pediatric infectious disease patients, conventional way (teleconsultation is created in written form by the resident ± a pharmacist, and afterwards modified and corrected by a pediatric infectious disease specialist)

Arm 2: At a later time and without being used for patient treatment: Generation of a teleconsultation by a specialised in-house large language model (LLM), modified and corrected by a pediatric infectious disease specialist

Arm 3: Consultation that was generated in arm 2 by a specialised in-house large language model (LLM). This consultation is only used for research purposes in order to compare different LLM-versions (no use in patient care).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All written infectious disease consult requests from the cooperating clinics are eligible for inclusion, provided they concern patients from birth until they reach their 18th birthday. The requests must include information on the patient's medical history, vaccination status, physical examination findings, prior diagnostics and therapy, as well as the specific question to the infectious disease team.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria are questions relating to specialties other than pediatric infectious disease, as well as lack of consent from the legal guardians for consultations or incomplete data.
